content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Tactical Network Communication (budget line 1989B11200) is a U.S. Army procurement program funded in the Other Procurement, Army account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "67f6eb38356b5c58"}}, {"text": "The line supports the Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) initiative to modernize command-and-control systems at the transport layer, delivering the latest commercial-off-the-shelf networking and communications capabilities to warfighters from home station to the most austere battlefield environments.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}, {"text": "The funding line consists of two distinct portfolios: the Signal Modernization (SIGMOD) Program and Tactical Network Technology Modernization in Service (TNT-MIS).", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}, {"text": "The SIGMOD portfolio augments, extends, and strengthens the tactical network with rapidly deployable, high-throughput, low-latency line-of-sight and beyond-line-of-sight capabilities, including mesh-enabled backhaul radios with low-probability-of-intercept and anti-jam features.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}, {"text": "In FY2025 this line consolidated the Signal Modernization Program (B00010) and the Tactical Network Technology Mod in Service (B07100/B07110) budget lines in response to FY24 Defense Appropriations language requiring consolidation options; it is not a new start, and funds were realigned to continue ongoing efforts.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's main FY2026 procurement request is $866,347 thousand (about $866 million) in Other Procurement, Army, all discretionary funding.", "citation": {"fact_id": "67f6eb38356b5c58"}}, {"text": "That main line was enacted at $378,645 thousand (about $379 million) in FY2025, so the FY2026 request is more than double the prior year.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9f61fbc33731b57c"}}, {"text": "A separate, much smaller line on the P-1R exhibit requests $12,798 thousand (about $12.8 million) for FY2026, down from $34,627 thousand enacted in FY2025.", "citation": {"fact_id": "bc7e3f6269728253"}}, {"text": "Within the request, the SIGMOD (Signal Modernization) program's FY2026 procurement dollars amount to $142.400 million, funding hardware such as line-of-sight backhaul radios, point-to-multipoint radios, broadband kits, secure wireless and secure cellular, TROPO-M, and TRILOS.", "citation": {"fact_id": "8f2f6aedcfc64e91"}}, {"text": "Beyond hardware, the SIGMOD funding also covers field and pipeline spares, post-deployment software support and licenses, contractor data, fielding and unit integration, and government and contractor management of the portfolio's systems.", "citation": {"fact_id": "8f2f6aedcfc64e91"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Army, with funding drawn from the Other Procurement, Army appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ea3018636e855b2a"}}, {"text": "The line is the Army's response to FY24 Defense Appropriations language requiring consolidation options for Other Procurement, Army budget lines, folding the former Signal Modernization Program and Tactical Network Technology Mod in Service lines into a single funding line.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}, {"text": "The effort directly supports the Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) initiative, the modernization program whose transport-layer requirements the SIGMOD and TNT-MIS portfolios are built to meet.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da66e1ceda6bb427"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
